audit.whatIsWrong: Two strings say the armour shred comes off a 'cannon-to-hammer swap' — spikes[0].text ('his first cannon-to-hammer swap shreds my Armor') and early ('his first hit after a cannon-to-hammer swap shreds my Armor'). The swap direction is backwards.
audit.why: Riot's own text: in Hammer Stance, R transforms into Mercury Cannon and 'the first attack in this form reduces the target's Armor and Magic Resist'; in Cannon Stance, R transforms into Mercury Hammer and 'the first attack in this form deals additional magic damage'. So the shred belongs to the first attack after swapping INTO cannon, and the hammer-form first hit is bonus magic damage instead. The Wiki puts the reduction at 20/25/30/35% by level for 5 seconds. A Nasus watching for the wrong swap will brace at the wrong moment — and worse, will think the shred is coming when Jayce closes to melee, which is when he is actually safest to Wither.
audit.corrected: Both strings and whys[1] now name Mercury Cannon and the correct direction, with the 5s duration.

audit.whatIsWrong: Thundering Blow appears three times but only ever as a knockback that costs a stack. Its damage type is never given.
audit.why: Thundering Blow deals 8 / 10.8 / 13.6 / 16.4 / 19.2 / 22% of the target's MAXIMUM health as magic damage before the 600-unit knockback. Nasus is the worst possible target for that: he builds health, and Fury of the Sands grants bonus Health on top, so his own two defensive levers both increase what this hit takes off him. It is also magic damage, so the armour in the recommended build does nothing against it. This is the biggest single omission in the matchup and it changes how the player should value R's bonus HP in a duel.
audit.corrected: Stated in breakdown.cooldowns, dontsFull, early, mid and wants.foe[1].

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns listed Shock Blast twice and gave no numbers for anything.
audit.why: Thundering Blow is 20/18/16/14/12/10 — by far the longest thing Jayce has in lane and the only cooldown worth actually waiting out, since Shock Blast comes back fast and the stance swap is a flat 6s. Telling a player to 'track Shock Blast' points them at the cooldown they cannot outlast.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns rewritten around the gate interaction and Thundering Blow's 20s.

audit.whatIsWrong: The two layers disagree on five of seven stages. full phases[].side reads Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Skill; content win[] reads Skill/Jayce/Jayce/Skill/Skill/Nasus/Nasus.
audit.why: The full layer's own stage text agrees with the content layer, not with its own sides — phases[4] says 'Fury of the Sands flips dives ... the stat-check runs your way' while scoring the stage to Jayce, and phases[6] says 'you out-duel Jayce on cooldown and three-shot his tower' while scoring it Skill. The content layer also explains why: Level 6 is a non-spike for Jayce because his R is the stance swap he already had, while Nasus gains lifesteal, size and resists.
audit.corrected: phases[3], [4] set to Skill and phases[5], [6] to Nasus, matching content win[] and each stage's own text. phases[3].why rewritten so the stage reads as the Wither equaliser rather than 'still Jayce's window'.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rated HARD, difficulty 7/10, on a lane Nasus wins 53.03% over 677 games whose own chart is Nasus 2 / Jayce 2 / skill 3.
audit.why: Nothing in the entry supports HARD once the early levels are over — the mid text calls level 6 a flat spot for Jayce and the late text calls the matchup his to lose. Poke lanes are uncomfortable, not losing.
audit.corrected: diff EVEN, diffRating 6/10, breakdown.difficulty and the final rating line aligned.

audit.why: suspectNames flagged "Spirit Fire's" in late. False positive — Spirit Fire is Nasus's real E name; the flag is the possessive apostrophe. No edit made.

edits.before: Still Jayce's window — respect Shock Blast fully. Passive lifesteal plus Fleet means he must commit hard to actually dent you; make those commits cost.
edits.after: Wither is the equaliser — it kills the Hextech Capacitor swap speed he kites with, so Levels 4-5 flatten out the moment your slow is up and he is stuck.

edits.before: - Jayce Shock Blast: matchup-defining — His main poke. Dodge it. Track it before every engage. - Jayce To the Skies! / Shock Blast: Hammer: leap + slow. Cannon: a long-range artillery line. Dodge or sidestep it.
edits.after: - Jayce Shock Blast: matchup-defining — fired through his gate it gets faster, longer and harder. Sidestep it. - Jayce Thundering Blow: 20s at rank 1, magic damage scaled off your MAXIMUM health, then a knockback.

edits.before: Burning your answer for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Thundering Blow is magic damage off your max health, then 600 units back.

edits.before: Levels 1-3 belong to Jayce and I just have to eat it. At Level 1 he only has one Cannon-Q, so I soak my Q farm and accept the poke while we're both weak. It gets worse at 2-3 when his E Acceleration Gate unlocks: a gated Shock Blast chunks me at full range, and his first hit after a cannon-to-hammer swap shreds my Armor every single time I walk up for a stack. Don't overcommit to a stack on a freezing wave or his E Thundering Blow knocks me off it and I lose the stack AND the XP. Last-hit with the tip of Q, take the poke, and trust that Soul Eater heals it.
edits.after: Levels 1-3 belong to Jayce and I just have to eat it. At Level 1 he only has one Cannon-Q, so I soak my Q farm and accept the poke while we're both weak. It gets worse at 2-3 when his E Acceleration Gate unlocks: a gated Shock Blast chunks me at full range, and his first attack after swapping into Mercury Cannon strips my Armor and MR for five seconds. Don't overcommit to a stack on a freezing wave or Thundering Blow knocks me off it — that hit is magic damage off my MAXIMUM health, so my own bulk feeds it. Last-hit with the tip of Q and trust Soul Eater.

edits.before: This is where I claw it back to even, so I trade smart around W. By Levels 4-5 I have a real stack count and Wither, and the second that slow lands his Hextech Capacitor swap speed is useless and he's stuck in a melee fight his squishy frame loses. So I only let him commit the gate-Q into swap into Hammer combo while my Wither is on cooldown, and I punish hard the moment he's in range with the slow up. Level 6 is a flat spot for him because his R is just the stance-swap he already had, while my Fury of the Sands hands me lifesteal, size and bonus resists, so this is where the lane stops being his.
edits.after: This is where I claw it back to even, so I trade smart around W. By Levels 4-5 I have a real stack count and Wither, and the second that slow lands his Hextech Capacitor swap speed is useless and he's stuck in a melee fight his squishy frame loses. So I only let him commit the gate-Q into swap into Hammer combo while my Wither is on cooldown. Respect Thundering Blow: 20 seconds at rank 1, and it takes a slice of my maximum health, so Fury of the Sands' bonus HP feeds it. Level 6 is still a flat spot for him — his R is only the stance-swap he already had.

notes: Thundering Blow is MAGIC damage scaled off max health. The recommended build in report[8] for this matchup is Frozen Heart plus Plated Steelcaps, i.e. all armour, which does nothing against that hit — and Fury of the Sands' bonus Health actively increases it. I have not changed the build, because I cannot verify current top-lane item meta from the kit files, but the itemisation line is worth a second look by someone who can.
